data.title: About us
data.intro: A family-run design-build company in Mission Viejo, remodeling Orange County homes since 2009.

children.text: Stud Construction started by rebuilding homes after floods and fires. Our president, Andrei Damian, spent those early years advocating for homeowners so they got a fair settlement from their insurance company, and a voice when they felt brushed aside.

A passion for design took the company into custom remodeling and design-build. Today we handle everything from a single bathroom to a complete rebuild, with the same crew leads on site every day and an office team that keeps every detail on track.
We still take disaster restoration work, and we still treat every project like it is our favorite one.

$media.alt: Vaulted kitchen with white cabinets, marble-topped gray island, brick backsplash and antique wood hutches

items.label: Years in construction for our president
Design, permits, and construction under one roof

members.name: Andrei Damian
members.bio: Andrei has more than two decades in construction. He began rebuilding homes after floods and fires, advocating for homeowners with their insurance companies, before taking Stud Construction into custom design-build. He keeps up with the latest design trends and treats every project as his favorite. Away from work he go-karts with his three kids, snowboards, mountain bikes, and travels.

members.name: Radu Birle
members.bio: Radu is a builder with more than 15 years of construction experience. You will usually find him in the field, managing projects and getting his hands dirty. He holds a degree in Finance and Business Administration from Cal State Fullerton, and his favorite moment is handing over the keys. Off the job he plays competitive sports, fishes, and camps with family and friends.

members.name: Alice Damian
members.bio: Alice leads marketing and recruiting, building the team of experts and craftsmen behind every project. Her creative eye and love of luxury design shape the partners we bring in. Her favorite projects are the ones that turn the outdoors into living space. She spends her free time outside with her husband and three children.

members.name: Sunshyne Leland
members.bio: Sunshyne brings more than a decade of administration experience in construction and interior design. She coordinates the behind-the-scenes details that keep a remodel smooth and hassle-free. In her free time she knits, sews, roller skates, bakes, keeps houseplants alive, and takes on her own home improvement projects.

content.headline: Fire, water, and mold restoration

children.text: Damage from a natural disaster, a structure fire, water, or mold is stressful enough. We deal with your insurance company for you: we meet the adjusters they send to the site and negotiate the most equitable settlement for your loss.
Then we coordinate everyone involved, rebuild your home, and, if you want, take the chance to create the space you have always wanted.

items.quote: I hired Stud Construction to install a bar in my kitchen area, as well as updating the counter top, sink, faucet, and back splash in my 2nd bathroom. The quality of the work performed was good overall, Andrei and Kurt were great at communicating with me, and they completed the project on time. As a matter of fact, every person that worked on the project was very nice and communicated well. The only reason why I give them 4 out of 5 is that some of the details of the work could’ve been done a bit better. For example, their counter top guy could’ve done a better job with hiding the line in the counter tops where the stone comes together, (this line is virtually invisible in the counter tops that my builder installed,) and the pattern the tile back splash didn’t line-up perfectly. However, overall I would definitely recommend using them to others.
items.name: Brian Taber

items.quote:
In February of 2016, we had a house fire and needed a general contractor/ remodel after careful review of about 30 different companies who came to my home to give me business cards. I chose STUD CONSTRUCTION. It was the best choice I could have made.
The day after the fire I had a waiting line of claims adjusters, lawyers and construction representatives at my door. Each company was told the same thing.
Just leave me your card and I will check you out on BBB the California license board and the California court system for any lawsuits. Andrei and his company stood out as one of the best reviewed NO problems on any of those sights. Their initial representative had said to me “ YES check us out, by all means.”
The estimate went as well as can be expected. After we had 4 estimates Stud construction was closest to our insurance estimate almost to the dollar. We agreed to hire them and next day Andrei came out and had a thorough discussion of the project. Since we had to do this we also went with a lot of remodeling including two complete bathroom remodels. A kitchen remodels and removal of a load bearing wall this was in addition to the fire and smoke damage.
Andrei and his designer Kurt were great throughout this whole process. Very helpful informative and knowledgeable. I cannot say enough about their professionalism or the quality of the work.
They worked within our time schedule and had all the permits and even dealt directly with our mortgage company and insurance company. Stud Construction went above and beyond meeting my expectations the project was done BEAUTIFULLY and correctly. Andrei and Kurt are great guys to work with. It was always like working WITH them every step of the way we made decisions together. They would input an idea or we would and a plan would be done to do what we all thought was best.

data.title: Privacy
data.intro: How this site handles analytics and the information you send us.

children.text: This site uses anonymous, cookieless analytics to understand which pages are useful. It does not set cookies, store identifiers in your browser, or build a profile of you. Page addresses are recorded without query strings, except campaign tags such as utm_source.
When you send the contact form, we store your name, email, phone, project type, and message so we can reply. We do not sell or share this information, and it is used only to respond to you.
The contact form is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, which checks that a person, not a bot, is submitting it.
Our client portal is run by CoConstruct (Buildertrend), and our social profiles on Instagram, Facebook, and Houzz are run by those companies. Each has its own privacy policy.
To ask about or delete information you have sent us, use the contact form and mention this page.

children.text: A home in need of an update

With a focus on opening up space, we moved the kitchen so it flows into the rooms around it. The wall between the living room and kitchen came out, and the island was rotated for seamless indoor and outdoor entertaining.
An old under-stair wine cellar was removed and a built-in desk was constructed in its place.

Upstairs, the primary suite lost walls too. The walk-in closet became a double rain shower and steam room, a freestanding tub greets you at the door, and a 10-foot floating double vanity runs along one side. An accent wall of wood-look tile finishes the spa feel the owners were after.

children.text: Rebuilt after a fire

After a fire destroyed most of the upstairs, the homeowner took the chance to completely remodel the primary bathroom. First on the agenda was replacing an awkward, dated suite with something that felt like a spa.

Raising the wet area created a visual and physical separation between the shower and tub and the vanity and water closet. The step also let us install a linear drain, so there is no curb between the wet and dry areas.

children.text: Opened up for a full house

This home was built when rooms were segmented and restrictive. The family needed the floor plan to open up, and finishes that are easy to clean while showing off their modern style. Not one piece of the interior was left untouched.

The couple and their two girls are active in their church and often fill the home with guests of all ages. To make room, we moved the kitchen to the opposite side of a shared bathroom wall. The new space takes on many roles and reuses the existing plumbing.
Setting the island a little farther from the range than usual created a direct aisle from the entry through to the bedrooms and living room.
